de.title: Charlie Sheen bittet Rob Lowe nach Attacken um Verzeihung
de.description: Charlie Sheen (61) hat seinen langjährigen Freund und Schauspielkollegen Rob Lowe (62) wegen früherer Attacken im Netz um Verzeihung gebeten. Im Podcast "Mostly Sheen-ius" gestand der "Two and a Half Men"-Star jetzt, während seiner Suchtprobleme mehrere verletzende und ungerechte Beiträge über Rob veröffentlicht zu haben. Rückblickend fand Charlie dafür klare Worte: "Und sie waren gemein und dumm." Die beleidigenden Kommentare stammen nach seinen Worten aus der Zeit vor dem 12. Dezember 2017. An diesem Tag habe er nach eigenen Angaben mit Drogen und Alkohol aufgehört. Umso überraschender fiel Robs Reaktion auf die Entschuldigung aus. Die Attacken von damals seien offenbar nie richtig bei ihm angekommen oder längst in Vergessenheit geraten. Statt seinem Freund die damaligen Äußerungen nachzutragen, habe der Schauspieler darauf vertraut, dass Charlie eines Tages einen anderen Umgang mit seiner Abhängigkeit finden würde. Darüber hinaus habe Rob über viele Jahre hinweg immer wieder für Charlies Genesung gebetet.

mx.title: Edén Muñoz marca distancia tras la detención de Gabito Ballesteros en Querétaro: ‘Hay que dar un paso atrás’
mx.description: El cantautor sinaloense Edén Muñoz fijó su postura respecto a la reciente detención del intérprete Gabito Ballesteros en Querétaro, dejando en claro que ha decidido mantenerse al margen de las situaciones personales de sus colegas y respetar el proceso que atraviesa cada artista. Durante un encuentro con los medios de comunicación, el ex vocalista de Calibre 50 reveló que antes de que ocurriera el incidente —registrado tras la suspensión de un concierto de Ballesteros luego de interpretar el tema “AMG”— ambos habían sostenido una plática para coordinar futuros proyectos a través de sus respectivos equipos de trabajo. “En lo último que hablamos fue: ‘aquí nos vemos, conecta con el equipo, ya venimos hablando de eso un montón’”, relató Muñoz sobre su último intercambio con el joven cantante. ‘Son temas delicados... yo las suelto totalmente’ Al ser cuestionado sobre la situación legal y mediática que enfrenta Gabito Ballesteros, el intérprete oriundo de Los Mochis subrayó que, siempre que exista certeza de que la persona se encuentra bien, lo más prudente es evitar involucrarse. “La verdad es que yo he marcado mi línea; son temas delicados en los cuales, mientras se sepa que la persona está bien, está bien, hay que dar un paso atrás, a nadie nos conviene, y esa es la verdad, con todas sus letras”, afirmó de manera contundente. Muñoz añadió que sus propias experiencias personales le han enseñado a respetar los tiempos y reacciones de cada individuo frente a las adversidades, optando por no cargar con asuntos que escapan de su control: “Cada quien vive su proceso como le toca, cada quien reacciona como cree que está bien. Son cosas que, como no están en mis manos, yo las suelto totalmente”.

co.title: Murió Paolo Bulgari a los 89 años, el empresario que convirtió su joyería en símbolo del lujo
co.description: Murió Paolo Bulgari a los 89 años, el empresario que convirtió su joyería en símbolo del lujo angelica.ferrer Sáb, 21/11/2026 - 14:29 Créditos: redes sociales El mundo de la moda y la joyería está de luto por la muerte de Paolo Bulgari, empresario italiano y una de las figuras que contribuyeron a transformar el negocio familiar en una de las casas de lujo más importantes del mundo. Su fallecimiento fue confirmado este sábado 21 de noviembre de 2026 por su familia, a través de un comunicado. Bulgari murió a los 89 años, dejando una trayectoria marcada por la expansión internacional de la compañía fundada por su abuelo, Sotirio Bulgari, y por la consolidación de una marca que se convirtió en referente de la joyería italiana. En el comunicado, sus familiares lo describieron como "una figura extraordinaria" y resaltaron "su profunda humanidad y el talento de un empresario que amaba Italia y fue su embajador en el mundo". "Ha fallecido el joyero más grande de nuestro tiempo", expresó la familia al anunciar su muerte. ¿Quién fue Paolo Bulgari y cuál fue su papel en la empresa familiar? Paolo Bulgari pertenecía a la tercera generación de la familia fundadora de la reconocida casa de joyería italiana. Tras la muerte de Giorgio Bulgari en 1966, la dirección de la empresa pasó a sus hijos Gianni, Paolo y Nicola, nietos del fundador Sotirio Bulgari. En un principio, Gianni, el mayor de los hermanos, asumió un papel central en la administración de la compañía, acompañado por Marina Bulgari, hija de Costantino Bulgari. Sin embargo, durante la década de 1980, Paolo y Nicola adquirieron mayor protagonismo en la dirección empresarial, al asumir la presidencia y la vicepresidencia, respectivamente. En ese periodo, la familia confió la gestión operativa a Francesco Trapani, sobrino de los hermanos e hijo de Lia Bulgari. Trapani ingresó a la empresa en 1981 y fue nombrado director ejecutivo en 1984. Desde esa posición lideró durante casi tres décadas una etapa de transformación que permitió consolidar a Bulgari como uno de los grandes grupos internacionales del sector del lujo. Le podría interesar: Disney prepara el regreso de 'Mi Pobre Angelito' con Macaulay Culkin La expansión de Bulgari hacia los mercados internacionales Uno de los procesos más importantes en la historia de la compañía fue su crecimiento fuera de Italia. Desde la década de 1970, Bulgari comenzó a fortalecer su presencia internacional mediante la apertura de establecimientos en ciudades como Nueva York, París, Ginebra y Montecarlo. Esta expansión permitió que la marca italiana llegara a nuevos mercados y consolidara su reconocimiento entre los consumidores de productos de lujo. Con el paso de los años, la empresa también diversificó su catálogo. Aunque la joyería continuó siendo uno de sus principales negocios, la compañía amplió su oferta hacia relojes, accesorios, artículos de cuero y perfumes. El nombre de Bulgari, cuya identidad visual utiliza la letra V latina en lugar de la U, se convirtió en uno de los símbolos más reconocibles de la tradición joyera italiana. Durante la etapa de liderazgo de Paolo Bulgari y su familia, la compañía fortaleció su presencia internacional y amplió sus líneas de negocio. La venta de Bulgari al grupo francés LVMH Otro de los momentos determinantes en la historia de la empresa ocurrió en 2011, cuando Bulgari fue vendida al grupo francés de lujo LVMH. La operación tuvo un valor aproximado de 3.700 millones de euros, según la información de la Agencia EFE. La transacción marcó una nueva etapa para la compañía italiana, que pasó a formar parte de uno de los conglomerados más importantes de la industria mundial del lujo. La trayectoria de Paolo Bulgari quedó vinculada a ese proceso de crecimiento y transformación, que llevó a la empresa familiar a competir en los principales mercados internacionales. Le podría interesar: Yotzin, el hombre de 13.000 años hallado en un aeropuerto El legado social de Paolo Bulgari y los detalles de su funeral Además de su actividad empresarial, Paolo Bulgari desarrolló iniciativas relacionadas con el apoyo social. En 2019 creó la Fundación Paolo Bulgari, una organización dedicada a impulsar proyectos orientados a combatir la desigualdad y la pobreza. La iniciativa reflejó una faceta de su trayectoria que trascendió el sector empresarial y buscó contribuir al bienestar de comunidades vulnerables. Tras confirmarse su fallecimiento, la familia informó que las honras fúnebres se realizarán el próximo lunes 23 de noviembre, a las 11:00 de la mañana, en la Basílica de Santa Croce in Gerusalemme, en Roma. Con su muerte, la industria del lujo despide a uno de los empresarios que participaron en la transformación de Bulgari, una compañía que pasó de ser un negocio familiar italiano a convertirse en una marca reconocida internacionalmente. ve.title: GOBERNADORA DEL DISTRITO 4380 DE ROTARY INTERNATIONAL VISITÓ EL ARCHIVO ZUBILLAGA EN CARORA
ve.description: La gobernadora del Distrito 4380 de Rotary International, Auristher Pinto, acompañada por miembros del Rotary Club Carora, realizó este jueves 19 de noviembre una visita institucional al Archivo Zubillaga con el propósito de conocer de cerca el patrimonio documental que resguarda este repositorio histórico en el municipio Torres. La presentación de la colección —integrada por fotografías, publicaciones hemerográficas, correspondencias y documentos de alto valor histórico— estuvo a cargo de su custodio, el ingeniero Cruz Mario Zubillaga. Durante la jornada, el anfitrión condujo un recorrido cronológico que abarcó desde la llegada del primer miembro de la familia Zubillaga a Carora y la formal instalación del archivo por parte de Cecilio “Chío” Zubillaga Perera, hasta su gestión en la actualidad. En el transcurso de la exposición, Cruz Mario Zubillaga resaltó los vínculos históricos entre el Archivo y el movimiento rotario local. Como testimonio de esa afinidad, exhibió el primer Libro de Actas de Reuniones Semanales del Interact Club (1964-1977), agrupación juvenil auspiciada por Rotary y fundada por el doctor Pablo Álvarez Yépez, quien, al igual que Cecilio Zubillaga Herrera, fue miembro rotario y custodio de este fondo documental. Al cierre del encuentro, la abogada Danny Gómez expresó el agradecimiento institucional a la directiva del Rotary Club Carora por la donación de la serie Obras Completas dedicada a Cecilio Zubillaga. Destacó que esta colección pertenece a una de las subdivisiones editoriales de la Biblioteca de la Academia Nacional de la Historia de Venezuela, orientada a recopilar y preservar la producción intelectual íntegra de destacados historiadores, ensayistas y pensadores venezolanos. Asimismo, precisó que, por iniciativa del entonces director de la Academia Nacional de la Historia, Guillermo Morón, la vida y obra de Chío Zubillaga inauguró esta serie editorial mediante una compilación organizada por Ramón Querales y publicada en Caracas entre 1988 y 1993. La obra consta de nueve volúmenes distribuidos en estudios históricos (tomos 1 y 2), correspondencia (tomos 3 y 4), el índice de su archivo (tomo 5), temas sociales y económicos (tomos 6 y 7) y temas políticos (tomos 8 y 9), además de la biografía de Chío Zubillaga escrita por Juan Páez Ávila, conformada por dos tomos. Con este intercambio institucional, el Archivo Zubillaga continúa fortaleciendo las alianzas destinadas a la preservación, el estudio y la difusión de la memoria historiográfica y cultural de Carora. Nota de prensa: Archivo Zubillaga.-

in.title: Hunger Games Sunrise On The Reaping Ending Explained: How does Haymitch Abernathy become cynical after his initial rebellion?
in.description: Disclaimer: This article contains spoilers. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is the latest instalment in the movie franchise, which was released in theaters on November 20, 2026. Starring Joseph Zada and Mckenna Grace in the lead roles, the film also has Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Maya Hawke, Ben Wang, and more in key roles. If you have watched the film in theaters this week and are wondering about the ending, here is an explainer to help you out. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Ending Explained Set 24 years before the events of the original Hunger Games trilogy, Sunrise on the Reaping follows a young Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) as he enters the brutal 50th Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell. On his 16th birthday, District 12 is required to send four tributes instead of the usual two. When the selected tribute, Woodbine Chance, attempts to escape and is shot, Haymitch is forced to take his place after trying to protect his girlfriend, Lenore Dove Baird. In the Capitol, Haymitch and fellow District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) receive guidance from former victors Wiress and Mags. Meanwhile, Beetee and cameraman Plutarch Heavensbee secretly recruit Haymitch into a rebel plan to ruin the arena's underground systems. Inside the arena, Haymitch teams up with Beetee's son, Ampert, to trigger the explosives and flood the underground network. Although their plan briefly disrupts the power supply, it fails to bring the Games to an end. Ampert is subsequently taken down by mutts, while President Snow triggers a volcanic eruption that eliminates several remaining tributes. Haymitch eventually wins the competition after using the arena's force field against his final opponent, Silka from District 1. However, his victory comes at a devastating cost. To punish him for his rebellion, Snow manipulates the narrative through edited broadcast footage, portraying Haymitch as a selfish and ruthless victor rather than someone who challenged the Capitol. Upon returning to District 12, Haymitch discovers that his home has been burned down and his mother and younger brother, Sid, have passed away. Although Lenore Dove (Whitney Peak) is eventually released from Peacekeeper and reunites with him, their happiness is short-lived. She eats red gumdrops that she believes Haymitch gave her, unaware that Snow has secretly poisoned them. Lenore Dove passes away in Haymitch's arms, leaving him completely devastated. With everyone he loves taken away and his reputation manipulated by the Capitol, Haymitch withdraws from society and settles into isolation in Victors' Village. He eventually turns to alcohol, becoming the bitter and cynical mentor we first encounter in The Hunger Games, 24 years later. The film concludes with an epilogue set after the events of Mockingjay. An older Haymitch, played by Woody Harrelson, celebrates his birthday alongside Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson). Unlike his earlier birthdays, this one passes without a Reaping, symbolising the end of the Games and the Capitol's control over the districts. Having finally fulfilled his promise to Lenore Dove to help bring the Hunger Games to an end, Haymitch sits peacefully on the hill where they once shared memories. in.title: 25 films selected from 404 entries for Indian Panorama
in.description: Panaji, Nov 21: A total of 25 feature films have been selected from 404 entries for the Indian Panorama 2026 at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), with the jury highlighting the diversity of stories and cinematic traditions across the country. Addressing a press conference in Goa, filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar, who chaired the Feature Film Jury, said the selection process was enriching, with films spanning different genres and languages. He said the jury was satisfied with its final choices and particularly recalled some Marathi, Ladakhi and Malayalam films that made a strong impression. Senior columnist and jury member Bharathi Pradhan said the panel focused on originality and representation, ensuring that the selection reflected perspectives from across the country. Actor and jury member Bindu Chandramouli said films from different regions shared common human emotions despite differences in language and style. She encouraged audiences to explore films beyond their linguistic preferences. Cinematographer M S Prabhu described the selection process as a virtual tour of India, while jury member K S Sivaraman said some films had compelling stories that could appeal to audiences beyond their regions. Jury member Soham P Shah said the message conveyed by a film was among the factors considered during selection. The selected feature-film package comprises 20 films in the Indian Panorama section and five in the Mainstream Cinema section. The selection of the five mainstream films was also made collectively, based on their concepts, ideas and potential, Bhandarkar said. Aditya Dhar's Hindi film Dhurandhar has been selected as the opening feature film of Indian Panorama 2026. The wider Indian Panorama selection also includes 20 non-feature films. sg.title: HEARTBOT AI Wins Chunghwa Telecom Special Award at Meet Neo Star 2026
sg.description: Named to the top 30 from more than 200 startups, AnyInsight won over judges with its zero-trust approach to AI governance TAIPEI, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HEARTBOT AI has won the Chunghwa Telecom Special Award at Meet Neo Star 2026, the startup competition held during the Meet Taipei Startup Festival. CEO Nathan Yen pitched AnyInsight, the company's enterprise AI security and governance platform, at the Meet Neo Star Demo Show Final on November 20, showing judges how companies can expand their use of AI agents without losing control of their data. HEARTBOT AI receives the Chunghwa Telecom Special Award from a representative at Meet Neo Star 2026 Alongside the judges' awards, sponsors selected startups from the top 30 for their own prizes. HEARTBOT AI received the Chunghwa Telecom Special Award from Chunghwa Telecom (CHT), which includes priority eligibility for the final selection of the CHT 5G Accelerator Batch 9, CHT hicloud credits and opportunities to connect and collaborate with CHT business units. Meet Taipei ran November 19 to 21 at Taipei Expo Park and drew more than 550 startups from 23 countries, its largest edition to date. In October, AnyInsight also received the ASOCIO Global Business Service Award. Companies Want AI Agents, and Proof They Are Under Control AI is moving beyond chat toward agents that read data, call internal systems and complete multistep tasks on their own. That changes what companies ask. The question is no longer which AI tools to use, but who can use them, what data they touch and what the agents actually did. The gaps are already showing. Employees use personal AI accounts for work, leaving no company record. Agents built by individual teams run without IT's knowledge, sometimes long after the people who built them have left. When auditors ask for AI usage records, teams spend weeks pulling them together by hand. Regulation is adding pressure. The transparency obligations in Article 50 of the EU AI Act began applying in August 2026, and for Taiwanese companies that operate internationally, AI governance is now part of day-to-day operations. One Platform for Models, Agents and Automated Workflows AnyInsight is a zero-trust enterprise AI security and governance platform. Companies can build agents and automated workflows in a single environment, drawing on over 20 leading cloud models, 350-plus ready-to-use AI agents and more than 500 application connectors. Every AI interaction passes through a zero-trust generative AI firewall, which uses context-aware semantic analysis to detect personal, financial and health data as well as cloud credentials, and can alert on, block or mask that content in real time. Before an agent calls a tool through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), AnyInsight checks policy and authorizes access by role under the principle of least privilege. High-risk actions require human approval, and every event is logged as exportable audit evidence. AnyInsight Edge Takes Governance On-Premises On November 12, HEARTBOT AI announced AnyInsight Edge, which extends the same governance to on-premises environments and AI servers. Many companies bound by data residency rules or regulation have already deployed private large language models, only to find them stuck as internal chatbots with no access to core systems such as ERP, MES and CRM. Edge ships as a container, needs no GPU and can run in a company's data center or integrate with an AI server's operating system. A single control plane manages policy centrally and enforces it consistently across cloud and on-premises environments. On-premises models such as Gemma and Mistral get access to AnyInsight's agents, automated workflows and connectors, while AI conversations, transferred data and audit logs can stay in-house. "Companies stopped asking whether to use AI a while ago," said Nathan Yen, CEO of HEARTBOT AI. "What holds them back is that once agents multiply, nobody can say for sure what data they touched or what they did. AnyInsight gives every AI interaction and every agent action an owner and a record. Once companies can see that, they're willing to put AI into their core operations." "Recognition from the Meet Neo Star judges means a lot to a startup working on AI governance," Yen said. "A growing number of companies now treat control as a condition for adopting AI, and that's the problem we work on every day." About HEARTBOT AI HEARTBOT AI develops trustworthy, high-assurance enterprise AI solutions. Its flagship platform, AnyInsight, is a zero-trust enterprise AI security and governance platform with a built-in generative AI firewall, role-based access control (RBAC) and auditable activity logs. AnyInsight helps organizations protect sensitive data and enforce AI governance across platforms and networks. Enterprises can securely and rapidly connect their data and business applications, adopt AI agents and automated workflows to boost productivity and knowledge management, and keep complete records ready for compliance audits. AnyInsight is certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 for information security management, and its AI governance and data protection mechanisms are designed on the principles of the EU AI Act and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). ph.title: Sofronio Vasquez takes success one step at a timespan class="Apple-converted-space"
ph.description: When Sofronio Vasquez won “The Voice USA” Season 26 in 2024, he gained international recognition and opportunities he had long hoped for. But before that victory, he had spent years joining singing competitions, facing rejection and trying to find his place in the music industry. At a press conference ahead of his recently concluded concert at the Proscenium Theater, the Filipino singer looked back on the struggles that led him to pursue music abroad and how his victory changed his life. He also spoke about learning to decide at his own pace which opportunities to pursue. Vasquez said he may now be performing for bigger audiences, but he still considers himself a growing artist who has a lot to prove. “I’m not perfect. I’m still growing as an artist and as an individual. But as much as possible, I really want to remain kind and keep my feet on the ground,” he humbly shared. The 34-year-old admitted that recognition could easily change a person’s perspective, especially when opportunities begin coming one after another. He makes a conscious effort not to let success get in the way of how he treats people and does not see the need to distance himself from the public just because more people now recognize him. “Sometimes I miss being alone, so there are times when I take the MRT or go to the mall. I understand that other artists have security reasons for keeping their distance, and I respect that. But personally, when people see me and approach me, I feel proud that they recognize me. I don’t want to hide. The more they see me, the more they get to know me, and I’m happy with that,” he said. While he appreciates the recognition, Vasquez is also aware of the criticism that comes with being in the public eye. He has read comments calling him arrogant and questioning how long his popularity will last, but he chooses to focus on his work rather than the criticism. “I don’t consider myself famous. I consider myself someone who is still working. If people call me famous, thank you. But if they don’t, that’s fine, too. I still have room to grow, and I still have a lot to prove to audiences. I will continue making music,” he said. For him, winning a competition does not automatically mean an artist has already made it. He believes the work must continue even after the awards. Before the recognition Before the international competition, Vasquez had already tried different paths. He described himself as an achiever who took on leadership roles while growing up in Ozamiz City, Misamis Occidental. “I have been blessed with many opportunities in life. I started being a leader in school. I was an achiever, and I was even elected city federated president of the SK (Sangguniang Kabataan). Not many people know that about me. I also studied dental medicine. I have tried different extremes in life,” he proudly shared. His decision to pursue dentistry came from a desire to establish a stable profession. Music, however, remained part of his life. He eventually joined singing competitions, including “Tawag ng Tanghalan,” where he continued to test his abilities as a performer. But the road he embarked on was not easy. Vasquez recalled receiving numerous rejections and reaching a point when he became tired of trying to establish himself in the local music industry. Looking back, he joined “The Voice Philippines” in 2014, but none of the coaches turned their chairs during his blind audition. He then tried his luck in “Tawag ng Tanghalan” in 2016, during the competition’s inaugural season on “It’s Showtime.” He won his daily elimination round but lost the following day. He returned for another attempt in 2017 (Season 2), eventually becoming a semifinalist and finishing seventh overall in June 2018. He tried again in November 2019 through “Tawag ng Tanghalan: All-Star Grand Resbak,” where he finished third. “People sometimes think that when you want something, you can get it immediately. But I have experienced so many rejections. I have heard no so many times. You don’t always know where you stand, especially when there are so many talented singers in the Philippines. You also don’t know how to market yourself or make people notice you,” he said. He eventually decided to move to the United States, partly to continue his dental career. He found an opportunity to study and work there, giving him another direction when pursuing music in the Philippines became difficult. “It wasn’t that I completely gave up on singing. There just came a point when I became tired. That’s why I tried moving to America because I also wanted to continue my dental career. I found an opportunity there to go to school and pursue it,” he said. Even while working, however, music continued to find its way back into his life. Vasquez recalled being reminded one day that he could still sing. He eventually set an audition date for “The Voice USA” and waited for the call that would change his career. “I set an audition date, and then I got the call. It took six months of waiting before that happened, and then I won the competition,” he said. The family behind the dream Beyond the career milestones, Vasquez’s story is also closely tied to his family and the financial difficulties they experienced. “Looking back, I believe everything happened for a reason. Those experiences built something in my heart. They taught me that I have no reason to complain because everything can disappear in an instant. You can have something today, and tomorrow it can be gone,” he said. One of the biggest changes his success brought has been his ability to provide for his mother and give his family a more comfortable life. During the pandemic, he recalled how they experienced financial difficulties and had to rely on government assistance. He also made biko (sweet rice cake), which was sold to help them get by. Now, he can afford things that were once difficult for them to have. “I am proud to say that when my mother asks me to buy groceries, I can now afford to do it. Sometimes I joke with her that we should not become too ambitious because if we do, we might end up struggling again,” he said. He also shared that he was able to buy a car and that his family now has a house of their own. “Those are the investments I have made in my life. We used to rent, and our house was surrounded by water underneath. When the water rose, it was frightening. You didn’t know when you might be told that the place would be demolished. Now, I am happy that we have a car and a house we can call our own,” he said. Despite the improvements in their circumstances, Vasquez said he remains mindful of the people who helped him along the way. His father’s advice, in particular, continues to guide him. “My father always reminded me not to forget to be kind. Nobody is perfect, but you should never forget to be good to other people. Kindness eventually comes with respect and love,” he said. Learning to navigate a new career Winning “The Voice USA” gave Vasquez opportunities beyond what he had experienced in local singing competitions. It also gave him the confidence to approach people and ask for opportunities he might previously have been too shy to pursue. He said one of the biggest changes in him as a performer was learning to speak up for himself. “Before, I would think that maybe I could do something, but I was too shy to ask. Now, I have the confidence to message my handlers and ask if I can be part of a production or an opening number. I can approach people and tell them what I want to do,” he said. He cited his opportunities to perform on “It’s Showtime” and “ASAP” as examples of how he has become more confident about taking initiative. He also remains grateful to the people who supported his career, including his “The Voice USA” coach, Michael Bublé. Vasquez said they continue to communicate even after the competition. They even had a recent video call in which Bublé invited him to an event he could not attend. But their conversations are not limited to music. Vasquez said Bublé also shares stories about his family, including his children. “He is very personal with me. We talk about family matters, and he shares what is happening with his children. We still have a connection. Even now, when I message him, he replies,” he said. Vasquez admitted that he still addresses the international singer as “Sir,” even though Bublé is not accustomed to being called that. He also recalled Bublé telling him that he misses performing in Asia and hopes to return in the future. Saying no to opportunities While his victory opened doors, Vasquez has also learned that accepting every opportunity is not necessarily the best decision. One of the most significant offers he received was an invitation to join the Broadway production of “Hamilton,” where he was offered the role of Aaron Burr. He confirmed that the invitation was legitimate after consulting theater professionals and Filipino artists familiar with the production. However, he eventually turned it down because he felt he needed more preparation before taking on such a demanding role. “I wanted to be part of it, but I also wanted to take calculated risks. I didn’t want to go there as a newcomer without the proper discipline and preparation. I know there is training, but I also know that the discipline required in theater is different,” he said. He explained that working in musical theater requires a different set of skills, particularly in acting, stage performance and communication. He has great respect for theater performers and wants to learn more about the discipline before accepting a role of that scale. For now, he hopes to get an opportunity to be part of a musical in the Philippines. “I really have a dream of being part of a musical. I want to learn that discipline because it is different from what we do as singers onstage. I have a high respect for theater artists, and I want to experience that kind of work,” he said. He added that he remains in communication with the casting office and understands that the opportunity may still be available when he is ready. For Vasquez, declining an offer does not necessarily mean closing a door. “I also believe that saying no is sometimes like saying yes. You cannot just say yes to everything and then arrive there without being prepared,” he said. Building music beyond the competition Vasquez is also working on original music and collaborations as he continues developing his career in the Philippines and the United States. He recently spent a week in Nashville, Tennessee, where he met producers and songwriters and participated in recording sessions. He explained that the process involves working with musicians, creating material and eventually choosing songs that could be included in a future release. “I don’t think there is a formula for making a hit song. What I am doing now is collaborating and attending sessions with musicians, especially in America. You go to the studio, meet producers and songwriters, record and create something together. Eventually, you have material that you can choose from,” he said. He has also been pitching ideas to Filipino producers and songwriters, including Jonathan Manalo and Rox Santos. Vasquez believes artists should continue creating and releasing music without becoming too focused on whether every song will become a hit. He cited songs that may not have received much attention when first released but eventually found an audience years later. “Once you release a song, you should literally release it. Don’t keep worrying about whether it will become a hit. You never really know the formula. As musicians, you just have to keep creating, release your work and perform whenever there is an opportunity,” he said. He also hopes to collaborate with Filipino rock musicians, including Rico Blanco, Jay of Kamikazee and Chito Miranda of Parokya ni Edgar. He also mentioned wanting to try rap with Gloc-9 and is equally open to working with younger artists, including Ben and Ben, Cup of Joe and P-Pop groups such as BINI. “I love different kinds of music. I don’t want to limit myself to one genre. If I have the opportunity to collaborate with different artists, whether they are established musicians or new performers, I will take it because it is also a chance for me to learn,” he said. A concert on his own terms Vasquez’s concert at the Proscenium Theater marked another important step in his career, but he admitted he was initially hesitant when his management at ABS-CBN offered him the opportunity. He was concerned about the financial risks involved, particularly with the challenges of producing concerts and selling tickets in the current economic climate. “I was really hesitant because I was personally afraid. I also wanted to be aware that the industry is difficult right now. I didn’t want my management to take a risk just because I wanted to have a concert, only for us to find out that we could not fulfill what we had planned,” he said. Instead of immediately pursuing a bigger production, he suggested starting with an intimate show. He described the concert as a way to show what he could do as a performer and prove to his management that he was ready for the next step. “I thought of it like a student presenting a thesis. I wanted to show that if you wanted to produce a bigger concert for me in the future, this is what I could do. If we could make the Proscenium show work, then I would have more confidence moving forward,” he said. Vasquez also took an active role in conceptualizing the production. He worked on the script, stage design, visuals, poster and camera placements, while coordinating with the people involved in putting the show together. The show featured several guest artists, including Ogie Alcasid, Jed Madela and National Artist for Music Ryan Cayabyab, among others. Vasquez said he was grateful that established performers readily agreed to join him. The sold-out show gave him confidence that he could eventually take on a larger production. Still, he knows that a bigger venue requires more than a successful competition and a growing following. He hopes to headline a concert at the Araneta Coliseum someday, but he understands that having a hit song could help make that possible. “I believe that I will continue singing as long as I can. Hopefully, I will have the opportunity to release a hit song, and that can also help me have a bigger concert. I am hopeful and positive that it will happen. If not as a solo performer, perhaps I can be part of a major concert with other artists,” he finally said. His Christmas wish, he said, had already come true with the sold-out Manila concert. Looking ahead, he hopes for more opportunities to work with fellow artists, explore collaborations and take on projects beyond singing, including acting and musical theater.

sa.description: أعادت دورة ريم الخيرية ذكرى الراحلين حسين علي حمود الحدري ومحمد هادي الرهوي، حيث تضم ثمانية فرق وزعت على مجموعتين وعلى الملعب الترابي بعرج حنشة، وبمشاركة مجموعة من أساطير الزمن الجميل من كبار فريق ريم.وفاء لا يموتمن هنا من قلب ريم، ومن على أرضية الملعب الترابي في عرج حنشة، حيث البساطة تصنع الجمال، والمحبة تصنع الحدث، والوفاء يصنع التاريخ، انطلقت قصة دورة مختلفة، دورة لم يكن هدفها الكأس فقط، بل كان هدفها تخليد الذكرى، وفي أجواء جميلة وربيعية وحماسية، تشرفت هذه الليلة بزيارة إلى ريم، وتحديدًا إلى الدورة الخيرية المقامة على الملعب الترابي في عرج حنشة.ثمانية فرقوأوضح القائمون والمنظمون على الدورة أنها أُقيمت وفاءً وعرفانًا، لتعيد ذكرى الراحلين: حسين علي حمود الحدري، ومحمد هادي الرهوي، رحمهما الله، وتضم ثمانية فرق، موزعة على مجموعتين، كل مجموعة تضم 4 فرق، تتنافس بشرف، وتتسابق على العطاء، قبل أن تتسابق على الأهداف، وأشاروا إلى أنه وما زاد هذه الدورة جمالًا وهيبة، هو مشاركة مجموعة من أساطير الزمن الجميل، من كبار فريق ريم، موزعين على الفرق الثمانية، ليعودوا إلى الملعب الذي صنعوا فيه المجد، وليمنحوا الجيل الجديد درسًا في الروح والانتماء والوفاء.

iq.title: شيوخ صلاح الدين للزيدي: أعيدوا نازحي العوجة والمناطق الأخرى إلى ديارهم
iq.description: شفق نيوز- صلاح الدين أعلن رئيس مجلس عشائر صلاح الدين، جاسم الجبارة، باسم شيوخ ووجهاء ومثقفي المحافظة، تأييدهم لإجراءات الحكومة الاتحادية برئاسة رئيس الوزراء علي فالح الزيدي في مكافحة الفساد وحصر السلاح بيد الدولة وتعزيز الأمن، داعياً في الوقت ذاته إلى الإسراع بإنهاء ملف النزوح وإعادة العائلات إلى مناطقها. وقال الجبارة، لوكالة شفق نيوز، إن عودة النازحين إلى ديارهم في العوجة ومناطق تل الذهب وسليمان بيك وعزيز بلد والرفيعات أصبحت ضرورة ملحة، بعد سنوات طويلة أثقلت كاهل العائلات وأبعدتها عن منازلها وأراضيها ومصادر رزقها. ورحب بصدور الأمر الديواني رقم (251214) في 7 أيلول 2025، والمتضمن تشكيل لجنة برئاسة رئيس هيئة الحشد الشعبي فالح الفياض وعضوية الجهات الأمنية والخدمية المعنية، لتحديد موعد عودة النازحين في العوجة والمناطق الأخرى، وإعادتهم على شكل وجبات بفاصل زمني قدره عشرة أيام بين كل وجبة، إلى جانب تحديد جهة ماسكة جديدة واستئناف الخدمات في المناطق المشمولة. وأكد الجبارة أن صدور الأمر يمثل خطوة مهمة طال انتظارها، لكنه شدد على ضرورة الانتقال من القرارات إلى التنفيذ الفعلي على الأرض، والإسراع بعودة العائلات وفق إجراءات آمنة ومنظمة وضوابط قانونية واضحة. وطالب الحكومة الاتحادية وحكومة صلاح الدين والجهات الأمنية والخدمية المعنية بضمان أن تكون العودة طوعية وآمنة وكريمة، من خلال تدقيق أمني فردي وعادل، بعيداً عن أي توظيف سياسي أو طائفي أو انتخابي للملف. وشدد على ضرورة عدم تعطيل عودة النازحين بحجة عدم اكتمال الإعمار والخدمات، داعياً إلى العمل بالتوازي على إعادة السكان واستكمال الخدمات، فضلاً عن الإسراع بصرف التعويضات ومعالجة ملفات الأملاك والأراضي وجبر الضرر وفق القانون. كما دعا إلى تعزيز المصالحة المجتمعية بخطاب وطني جامع يحترم تضحيات القوات الأمنية والحشد الشعبي وأبناء العشائر، وفي الوقت ذاته يراعي معاناة النازحين ويرفض الثأر والتحريض والتشهير الجماعي. وأشار الجبارة، إلى أن ملف النزوح لا ينبغي أن يقتصر على العوجة، مؤكداً وجود مناطق أخرى في صلاح الدين ما زال سكانها مهجرين، داعياً إلى اعتماد مبدأ موحد يشمل جميع المناطق، يقوم على عودة من يرغب بالعودة، وتعويض من يتعذر عليه ذلك، وإيجاد حلول عادلة لجميع العائلات. وختم بالقول إن المطلوب هو تحويل الأوامر والاجتماعات والوعود إلى إجراءات عملية ضمن جدول زمني واضح، وبشفافية أمام الرأي العام، بما يسهم في إغلاق ملف النزوح وإنهاء معاناة العائلات المهجرة.

iq.title: للمشاركة في احتفالات دينية.. البطريرك يوحنا العاشر يصل إلى موسكو
iq.description: وصل بطريرك أنطاكية وسائر المشرق للروم الأرثوذكس، يوحنا العاشر، إلى العاصمة الروسية موسكو، قادماً من دمشق، للمشاركة في احتفالات عيد الميلاد الثمانين لبطريرك الكنيسة الأرثوذكسية الروسية كيريل. وأعلنت الكنيسة الروسية أن البطريرك يوحنا العاشر وصل إلى موسكو، الأربعاء، برفقة وفد ضم عدداً من المطارنة ورجال الدين وشخصيات مدنية. وكان في استقباله في المطار المطران أنطوني، المسؤول عن العلاقات الخارجية في الكنيسة الروسية، والمطران نيفن صيقلي، ممثل بطريرك أنطاكية في موسكو، إضافة إلى نيكولاي بالاشوف، مستشار البطريرك الروسي كيريل، وعدد من رجال الدين. من رافق البطريرك يوحنا العاشر إلى موسكو؟ وضم الوفد المرافق المطران إلياس كفوري من صور وصيدا، والمطران أفرام معلولي من حلب، والأسقف بولس أوردولوأوغلو، إلى جانب عدد من رجال الدين، بينهم فيليب فاسيلتسف، ممثل الكنيسة الروسية لدى بطريركية أنطاكية، وبرثنيوس اللاطي وبولس دحدل. وضم الوفد المرافق للبطريرك عدداً من المطارنة ورجال الدين، إلى جانب شخصيات مدنية، بينهم السفير السوري السابق لدى روسيا حسان ريشة. علاقات بين الكنيستين السورية والروسية وتأتي الزيارة بعد لقاء جمع البطريرك يوحنا العاشر وفداً من الكنيسة الروسية، أواخر تشرين الأول الماضي، في دير سيدة البلمند في لبنان. وتناول اللقاء أوضاع المسيحيين في الشرق الأوسط والعلاقات بين الكنيستين، بالتزامن مع فعاليات دينية أقيمت في لبنان بمناسبة مرور 80 عاماً على تأسيس ممثلية الكنيسة الروسية فيه.

iq.description: شفق نيوز- نينوى انطلقت، يوم السبت، فعاليات المهرجان الثقافي والفني المركزي في محافظة نينوى، على قاعة البهو الملكي في المتحف الحضاري بمدينة الموصل. وقال وكيل وزارة الثقافة والسياحة، فاضل البدراني، لوسائل اعلام بينها وكالة شفق نيوز، إن "وزارة الثقافة استهلت فعالياتها الثقافية خارج العاصمة بغداد من محافظة نينوى، بتوجيه مباشر من وزير الثقافة ياسين العيثاوي، وذلك اعتزازاً بهذه المحافظة العريقة". وأضاف أن "المهرجان يعكس الصورة الحقيقية للموصل وإبداعات مثقفيها وفنانيها، بوصفها مدينة التنوع الثقافي والتآخي والإبداع والامتداد الحضاري الذي يجسد روح الهوية العراقية النابضة بالسلام والمحبة". وتابع أن "فعاليات المهرجان تتضمن إقامة معرض شامل للحرف اليدوية والصناعات التقليدية ذات الصلة بالتراث الثقافي المادي وغير المادي"، معرباً عن سعادته بوجود وفد الوزارة في نينوى لنقل رسالة الثقافة من بغداد إلى جمهور الموصل ومبدعيها وشبابها وحكومتها المحلية. وشدد وكيل الوزارة على أن "الحكومة العراقية، ابتداءً من رئيس مجلس الوزراء علي الزيدي، تولي اهتماماً بالغاً بحماية الموروث الثقافي والتراثي والآثاري في العراق، وتعمل بجدية على إنعاش الحركة الثقافية والفنية في نينوى وسائر المحافظات".

na.title: GTA 6 Made $3.79 Billion on Day One - IGN Daily Fix
na.description: In today's Daily Fix:As if anyone expected anything different, GTA 6 now has the biggest launch in entertainment history with a staggering $3.79 billion in sales in its first 24 hours. This includes more than 30 million pre-sale copies sold. And keep in mind, the PC version has yet to drop. Although GTA 6's launch dwarfs even the biggest movie releases, it's not a true 1:1 comparison as the game sells for about $80 a copy ($100 if you buy the ultimate edition), and your average movie ticket is nowhere near that expensive. In related news, prior to the launch of GTA 6, gamers spent 14% less this October than last year, despite heavy hitters like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and the Ocarina of Time remake dropping in the same month. This is likely due to the GTA 6 effect, and gamers wanting to save their time and money for that game instead. And finally, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey film helped boost sales of Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed Odyssey game. AC Odyssey, which was released in 2018, saw a spike in sales after the blockbuster movie debuted in July.

rw.title: GTA 6 Made $3.79 Billion on Day One - IGN Daily Fix
rw.description: In today's Daily Fix:As if anyone expected anything different, GTA 6 now has the biggest launch in entertainment history with a staggering $3.79 billion in sales in its first 24 hours. This includes more than 30 million pre-sale copies sold. And keep in mind, the PC version has yet to drop. Although GTA 6's launch dwarfs even the biggest movie releases, it's not a true 1:1 comparison as the game sells for about $80 a copy ($100 if you buy the ultimate edition), and your average movie ticket is nowhere near that expensive. In related news, prior to the launch of GTA 6, gamers spent 14% less this October than last year, despite heavy hitters like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and the Ocarina of Time remake dropping in the same month. This is likely due to the GTA 6 effect, and gamers wanting to save their time and money for that game instead. And finally, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey film helped boost sales of Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed Odyssey game. AC Odyssey, which was released in 2018, saw a spike in sales after the blockbuster movie debuted in July.

mg.title: LES BONS PLANS DU WEEKEND - L’embarras du choix
mg.description: Sorties en famille, spectacles musicaux et traditionnels, compétitions sportives : plusieurs rendez-vous attendent les Tananariviens ce week-end, entre détente, découvertes et divertissement. Envie de changer d’air, de s’amuser en famille, de retrouver les grandes voix malgaches ou de vibrer au rythme des compétitions sportives ? Ce week-end, les possibilités de sorties ne manquent pas dans la capitale et ses environs. Des espaces de loisirs d’Andakana aux scènes musicales, en passant par les terrains de sport, chacun pourra trouver une activité à son goût. Pour les familles en quête d’évasion, le Domaine d’Îlo, également connu sous le nom d’ILO Hôtel, figure parmi les destinations à retenir. Situé sur la route de Mahajanga, dans le secteur d’Andakana, à une trentaine de kilomètres d’Antananarivo, l’établissement accueille ses visiteurs dans un environnement verdoyant, entre rizières et collines. Son principal attrait réside dans la diversité des activités proposées. L’Aqua Park, avec ses piscines, ses toboggans, sa rivière artificielle et ses jeux d’eau, offre de nombreuses possibilités de divertissement aux enfants comme aux adultes. Les amateurs de sensations pourront, quant à eux, s’essayer aux balades en buggy, en quad ou aux sorties tout-terrain. Pour ceux qui privilégient le calme, l’établissement dispose également d’espaces dédiés au bien-être, avec spa, massages, hammam, sauna et jacuzzi. Des installations sportives, notamment des terrains de tennis, de basket-ball et de football, complètent les possibilités de loisirs. Des retrouvailles musicales et traditionnelles Dans un autre cadre, Gardénia Fitiavana, anciennement connu sous le nom d’Espace Fitiavana Andakana, constitue également une alternative pour ceux qui souhaitent profiter d’une journée en plein air. Situé à Andakana, cet espace de loisirs mise sur la convivialité et les activités familiales. Sa piscine extérieure représente l’une des principales attractions du domaine, tandis que les plus jeunes peuvent profiter des installations ludiques, notamment du trampoline et des espaces de jeux. Les visiteurs ont également la possibilité de s’installer dans les espaces verts aménagés pour un pique-nique ou un moment de détente. Entre baignade, jeux et déjeuner en plein air, Gardénia Fitiavana offre ainsi un cadre propice aux retrouvailles familiales et aux sorties entre amis. Pour les amateurs des grandes voix malgaches, le dimanche prendra une tout autre couleur, celle des retrouvailles musicales. Le retour de « Che Bel Canto », avec Samoela et plusieurs artistes féminines de différentes générations, figure parmi les rendez-vous attendus. Au Palais des Sports, le spectacle réunira notamment Monica Njava, Tosy et Ry Kiala Vazo autour du répertoire de Samoela. Le concept « Iaraka ampiram-peo amin’ny Samoela » promet des interprétations collectives, où les voix féminines viendront accompagner l’artiste dans ses propres chansons. Une occasion de redécouvrir des titres connus sous de nouvelles couleurs vocales et de retrouver des interprètes qui ont marqué différentes périodes de la scène musicale malgache. Entre nostalgie, complicité artistique et diversité des voix, ce rendez-vous s’annonce comme un moment de retrouvailles entre générations. Les amateurs de culture traditionnelle ont également rendez-vous à Ampefiloha pour une nouvelle confrontation de Hira gasy. Après la reprise remarquée des grandes rencontres le 15 novembre dernier, une nouvelle affiche est programmée ce dimanche, à partir de 10 heures, au kianja Rochel Rasamimanana. Les troupes Sahondrafinina Zanany de Fenoarivo et Rasamoelson d’Andohavary se mesureront à travers leurs chants, leurs danses, leurs discours et leurs expressions théâtrales. Issue d’une lignée artistique de trois générations, la formation Sahondrafinina Zanany se distingue notamment par la richesse de son répertoire vocal et ses grands chants narratifs, les « renihira ». En face, Rasamoelson d’Andohavary, troupe familiale attachée à la tradition de l’Imerina, mise particulièrement sur son dynamisme scénique et ses « dihy gasy ». Sa jeune chanteuse Sanni Miarantsoa contribue également à attirer un public plus jeune. Cette nouvelle rencontre s’inscrit dans la relance des représentations hebdomadaires, programmées jusqu’en décembre. Le sport aussi au rendez-vous Le retour du Hira gasy suscite déjà un réel engouement, au point que la capacité d’accueil du site, estimée à environ 700 personnes, ne suffit pas toujours à recevoir les spectateurs, dont le nombre peut dépasser le millier lors de certaines représentations. Les amateurs de sport ne seront pas en reste. Rugby, karting et basket-ball figurent également au programme, avec plusieurs rendez-vous à Antananarivo et ses environs. Le stade Makis d’Andohatapenaka sera particulièrement animé ce dimanche avec trois rencontres de rugby. Chez les dames, FTFA croisera le fer avec le SC Besarety, dans une confrontation qui promet de l’engagement. Deux autres affiches masculines compléteront le programme : TFA contre RCI, puis US Ankadifotsy face au RCSA. Une occasion pour les passionnés de retrouver l’ambiance du rugby local et de suivre les différentes formations en compétition. Les amateurs de vitesse auront également rendez-vous dimanche sur la piste du SRK à Imerintsiatosika. Le Trophée Faly Andrianafetra y réunira les pilotes de karting autour d’une nouvelle journée de compétition. De quoi offrir du spectacle aux passionnés de sports mécaniques. Le basket-ball ne sera pas en reste. Les présélectionnés des Ankoay sont attendus ce samedi matin pour une séance d’entraînement sur la route d’Imerinkasina. Ce rassemblement s’inscrit dans la préparation de la sélection nationale en vue de ses prochaines échéances. Entre les escapades aquatiques du côté d’Andakana, les retrouvailles musicales au Palais des Sports, les grandes joutes du Hira gasy à Ampefiloha et les compétitions sportives, ce week-end propose plusieurs façons de s’évader et de se divertir. Autant d’occasions de sortir du quotidien, de partager des instants avec ses proches et de profiter de la diversité des loisirs et des expressions culturelles et sportives malgaches. Cassie Ramiandrasoa / Donné Raherinjatovo

mg.title: LIONS INTERNATIONAL DISTRICT 417 - Cap vers le Nord
mg.description: Après le succès de la caravane humanitaire Lovasoa dans le Sud de Madagascar, le Lions International District 417 s’apprête à poursuivre son élan de solidarité en mettant le cap vers le Nord du pays. En octobre dernier, la caravane humanitaire Lovasoa a sillonné le Sud de Madagascar pendant neuf jours, portant assistance aux populations confrontées à une situation d’extrême urgence alimentaire. Sous la conduite du gouverneur du District 417, Stefan Andrianisa, et de son équipe, cette mobilisation solidaire a permis la distribution de paniers de vivres à plus de 850 foyers, représentant 2 100 bénéficiaires. Un périple de neuf jours qui a conduit la délégation à travers plusieurs villes et localités : Antsirabe, Mananjary, Nosy Varika, Manakara, Vohipeno, Vangaindrano, Tolagnaro, Amboasary et Ambovombe. Au-delà de l’aide alimentaire, cette caravane a été une véritable aventure humaine, faite de rencontres, de partage et de solidarité auprès des communautés les plus vulnérables. Fidèle à sa vocation humanitaire, le Lions International District 417 entend aujourd’hui poursuivre cette dynamique. Dans les prochains jours, la caravane Lovasoa reprendra la route, cette fois en direction du Nord de Madagascar. Cette nouvelle étape mobilisera à nouveau les Lions Clubs du District 417, grâce aux contributions des clubs issus de plusieurs territoires de l’océan Indien et d’ailleurs : notamment Madagascar, Maurice, La Réunion, Mayotte, Rodrigues et Djibouti. Cette mobilisation bénéficiera également de l’appui de généreux donateurs. Cette mobilisation collective témoigne de la force d’un réseau international uni autour d’une même ambition : agir concrètement pour les populations qui en ont le plus besoin. Lovasoa, une aventure humaine qui continue Bien au-delà d’une opération de distribution de vivres, la caravane Lovasoa traduit la volonté des Lions de faire de la solidarité un engagement concret, au service des communautés. Cette nouvelle expédition dans le Nord s’inscrit dans cette continuité, avec la même détermination à servir, à partager et à contribuer durablement au bien-être des populations rencontrées. Du Sud au Nord, un même esprit de solidarité anime le District 417, fidèle à son thème pour l’année 2026-2027 : « Agir ensemble, pour un héritage commun ». L'Express de Madagascar
